title: Everything Loss, or Surpassing Worth?
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: The power of this passage is not in the loss but in the surpassing worth of knowing Christ. Seen next to him, the rest is dead weight.
exhortation: I think I lose my way in this passage when I focus on the "everything as loss" part instead of the "surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus" part. The real truth is that knowing Jesus is far better than anything this world has to offer. It is our job to resist worldly pleasures, but the real power is found in being caught up in the glory of who Jesus is. When we see him for who he really is and find ourselves in an all-satisfying relationship with him, suffering loss feels more like casting off dead weight. Why would we want to carry around a bunch of rubbish?

But what about the good things in this world, like family, a good meal or a safe home? These are gifts from God, given to point us to the surpassing worth and glory of Christ. When we reverse it and make the good things the main thing, they leave us cold and depressed. Something goes wrong in our family and we get angry or fearful. We eat our favorite meal every day and get sick of it. We get the car of our dreams, and one scratch ruins our day. Jesus said it plainly: "Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it."

I recently read in Proverbs, "The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it." When we put the Lord first and love him with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, we find a truly blessed life: a blessing so deep that sorrow can't reach it, a joy so rich that suffering can't drain it, and a hope so strong that no enemy can topple it.
So are you afraid of losing something precious to you? The answer is to give it to Jesus and glory in who he is. He will make rich those who do, with a blessing that can't be taken away.
prayer: Lord, may we count it all as loss to know the surpassing worth of you, Jesus. Our lives on this earth are short. We are here for a moment, like grass that grows and withers the next day. So we offer our lives to you in spirit and truth, putting all our trust and hope in your finished work and your blood poured out for the forgiveness of our sins. We live in that, Lord Jesus.

Nothing we can say would sufficiently thank you for so great a salvation. That's why we'll spend eternity trying. The worship of Jesus in everything we do is the occupation of every Christian. May our lives reflect that as we go about our days, and may we live in your goodness and truth, Jesus. Amen.
